snippet.title: New York'taki Bu Sergi Herkesi Şaşırttı! 🤯
snippet.description:
Bütün bu insanlar ne arıyor?

Burası, sanatçı CJ Henry’nin New York’ta düzenlediği ücretsiz bir sanat sergisi. Sanatçı, boş bir galeriyi pastel renkli binlerce boncukla dolu devasa bir çukura dönüştürdü.

İçeri girdiğinizde size bir çift çorap, biraz ip ve gizlenmiş tüm tasarımları gösteren bir rehber veriliyor.

Ayakkabılarınızı çıkarıyor, çukurun içine giriyor ve aramaya başlıyorsunuz.

Boncukların arasına küçük karakterler, deniz canlıları, tek boynuzlu atlar ve onlarca farklı küçük tasarım gizlenmiş. Üstelik bazıları diğerlerinden çok daha nadir bulunuyor. 😱

İnsanlar kovalarını buldukları boncuklarla dolduruyor ve bunları iplere dizerek eve götürebilecekleri bileklikler ve kolyeler yapıyor.

Üst kata çıktığınızda ise tüm o gürültüden uzak, sessiz bir galeri bulunuyor. Burada aynı tasarımlar heykeller ve baskı eserler olarak sergileniyor. 🤯

snippet.title: 🥣🍂 HIGH-PROTEIN CARAMELISED PERSIMMON & COURGETTE OATS!! 🥒✨
snippet.description:
🥣🍂 HIGH-PROTEIN CARAMELISED PERSIMMON & COURGETTE OATS!! 🥒✨

🔥 375 CALORIES | 29G PROTEIN | 11G FIBRE

💚 Maximum Weight Loss Breakfast | High-Volume Vegan Recipe!

🔗 Click the LINK IN MY BIO for 100+ high-volume meals that helped me lose 66 lbs! ❤️

I PRESENT TO YOU… MY NEW BREAKFAST OBSESSION!! 😍

A MASSIVE bowl of creamy cinnamon porridge topped with sweet, caramelised persimmons and Greek-style soy yogurt!

And the BEST part?!

This entire enormous bowl contains just 375 CALORIES, 29G OF PROTEIN and 11G OF FIBRE! 🤯

THIS is how you do VOLUME EATING RIGHT!

For those of you who don't know, I'm a volume eater who lost 66 lbs while eating BIG, satisfying portions of delicious plant-based food.

And one of my favourite tricks is adding vegetables to absolutely EVERYTHING!

Including BREAKFAST! 😂🥒

Yes, we're making COURGETTE OATS!

Trust me, once you discover how much volume grated courgette adds to your porridge, you might never go back!

And because Thanksgiving is just around the corner, we're giving this breakfast a cozy, festive twist with cinnamon and caramelised PERSIMMONS! 🍂

✨ INGREDIENTS ✨

🥣 FOR THE CREAMY COURGETTE OATS:

🥒 Courgette, finely grated

🥣 About ⅓ cup oats

💧 Plenty of water

💪 Vegan protein powder

🍂 Cinnamon

🍊 FOR THE CARAMELISED PERSIMMONS:

🍊 Fresh persimmon

🍯 A little coconut sugar

🥄 FOR SERVING:

🌱 Greek-style soy yogurt

🍂 Extra cinnamon

👩‍🍳 HOW TO MAKE MY HIGH-PROTEIN PERSIMMON PORRIDGE:

1️⃣ GRATE YOUR COURGETTE! 🥒

Grab a courgette and grate it as finely as possible.

I usually remove the peel so my porridge doesn't turn green, but I completely forgot this time! 😂

Don't worry, it still tastes delicious!

2️⃣ MAKE YOUR CREAMY OATS! 🥣

Add about ⅓ cup of oats to a saucepan with your finely grated courgette.

Pour in plenty of water and start cooking!

The courgette softens into the oats, adding lots of extra volume without dramatically increasing the calorie density.

3️⃣ CARAMELISE YOUR PERSIMMONS! 🍊

While your oats are cooking, thinly slice a fresh persimmon.

Arrange the slices in a non-stick pan and sprinkle with a little coconut sugar.

Cook until beautifully golden, sweet and slightly caramelised!

These taste AMAZING with cinnamon porridge!

4️⃣ ADD YOUR PROTEIN! 💪

Once your oats are soft and creamy, stir in some cinnamon and vegan protein powder.

I'm currently working on building more muscle, so I love finding delicious ways to add extra protein to my meals!

The protein powder also makes the porridge sweet and creamy.

If you'd rather skip it, you can use maple syrup for sweetness instead, although the protein content will change.

5️⃣ MAKE IT EXTRA VOLUMINOUS! 💦

Here's one of my favourite volume-eating tricks!

Add MORE WATER!

Rather than making a tiny, thick portion of porridge, I add extra water to create a much BIGGER bowl.

Let it cook a little longer until everything is hot and creamy.

This is one of the simplest ways to increase food volume without adding lots of extra calories!

6️⃣ BUILD YOUR MASSIVE BREAKFAST BOWL! 😍

Grab your biggest bowl and pour in your creamy courgette oats.

Arrange those gorgeous caramelised persimmons on top.

Finish with a generous dollop of Greek-style soy yogurt and another sprinkle of cinnamon!

OH MY MUFFINS!! 🤤

It's warm, creamy, sweet, festive and SO satisfying!

✨ NUTRITION FOR MY ENTIRE BOWL ✨

🔥 Calories: 375

💪 Protein: 29g

🌱 Fibre: 11g

These are the macros for the version I made in the video. Your totals may vary depending on your ingredients and portions.

💚 WHY I LOVE THIS BREAKFAST

🥒 Courgette adds vegetables and extra volume.

🥣 Oats provide comforting, satisfying carbohydrates and fibre.

💪 Vegan protein powder boosts the protein content.

🍊 Persimmons add natural sweetness and a gorgeous festive flavour.

🌱 Soy yogurt makes everything extra creamy.

💦 Extra water helps create a BIGGER portion!

This is what low-calorie-density eating is all about!

I lost 66 lbs without giving up delicious food or forcing myself to eat tiny portions.

And I still LOVE experimenting with ways to make my meals bigger, more satisfying and more nutritious!

If you're looking for a cozy vegan breakfast that's perfect for the colder months, GIVE THIS ONE A TRY! 🍂❤️

Add about ⅓ cup of oats to a saucepan with your finely grated courgette.

Pour in plenty of water and start cooking!

The courgette softens into the oats, adding lots of extra volume without dramatically increasing the calorie density.

3️⃣ CARAMELISE YOUR PERSIMMONS! 🍊

While your oats are cooking, thinly slice a fresh persimmon.

Arrange the slices in a non-stick pan and sprinkle with a little coconut sugar.

Cook until beautifully golden, sweet and slightly caramelised!

These taste AMAZING with cinnamon porridge!

4️⃣ ADD YOUR PROTEIN! 💪

Once your oats are soft and creamy, stir in some cinnamon and vegan protein powder.

I'm currently working on building more muscle, so I love finding delicious ways to add extra protein to my meals!

If you'd rather skip it, you can use maple syrup for sweetness instead, although the protein content will change.

Add MORE WATER!

Rather than making a tiny, thick portion of porridge, I add extra water to create a much BIGGER bowl.

This is one of the simplest ways to increase food volume without adding lots of extra calories!

Grab your biggest bowl and pour in your creamy courgette oats.

Arrange those gorgeous caramelised persimmons on top.

Finish with a generous dollop of Greek-style soy yogurt and another sprinkle of cinnamon!

snippet.title: Nature Meets Engeneering 🤯 How Kingfisher Inspired Bullet Trains
snippet.description:
India is finally getting its first bullet train, with the Mumbai Ahmedabad High Speed Rail Project expected to begin operations in 2027. While Japan introduced the world's first high-speed bullet train, the Shinkansen, back in 1964, India is now preparing for a major transformation in railway transportation. But why do bullet trains look so different from regular Indian trains? Why does the Indian Railways locomotive usually have a flat front, while the Vande Bharat Express features an aerodynamic design and Japanese bullet trains have an extremely long pointed nose? There is an incredible scientific reason behind it!

The story begins in 1964 with Japan's first Shinkansen bullet train, which operated at speeds of up to 210 km/h. Although the Japanese high-speed railway was a revolutionary achievement, engineers soon discovered a serious problem. Whenever the bullet train entered a tunnel at high speed, it compressed the air inside, creating powerful pressure waves. These waves travelled through the tunnel and produced a loud sound similar to a sonic boom when they reached the exit. This phenomenon became known as the Tunnel Boom or Tunnel Micro-pressure Wave, and it was so powerful that nearby houses experienced disturbing noise and window vibrations.

To solve this unusual high-speed train engineering problem, Japanese engineer Eiji Nakatsu, who was also a birdwatcher, took inspiration from an unexpected source: the Kingfisher bird. He observed how a kingfisher dives into water at high speed to catch fish while minimizing water disturbance. Its unique streamlined beak inspired engineers to rethink the aerodynamic nose design of bullet trains. This is a fascinating example of biomimicry, where engineers copy designs and mechanisms found in nature to solve complex technological problems.

Inspired by the Kingfisher's beak, engineers developed a longer and more streamlined nose for Japan's Shinkansen trains. This aerodynamic bullet train design helped reduce pressure waves inside tunnels, minimize tunnel boom noise and improve the overall performance of high-speed railway systems. The innovation also demonstrated how aerodynamics, air resistance, train nose design and high-speed railway technology play an important role in modern transportation. From the Japanese Shinkansen E5 Series to advanced high-speed rail systems, the Kingfisher-inspired design became an iconic part of modern bullet train engineering.

Now, as India prepares for its first Mumbai Ahmedabad Bullet Train, an important chapter in Indian railway history is about to begin. The Mumbai Ahmedabad High Speed Rail Corridor, India's first high-speed rail project, is being developed with Japanese Shinkansen technology. While Indian Railways continues to modernize through Vande Bharat Express trains, modern locomotives, railway infrastructure upgrades and high-speed rail development, the upcoming Indian bullet train represents another major technological milestone. This is the fascinating science behind why bullet trains have such long noses and how a small bird helped inspire one of the biggest innovations in railway engineering
